# floodflow

**floodflow** is a map-first, climate-informed workflow for flood hazard
assessment in data-scarce basins. It chains rainfall extreme-value
analysis, rainfall–runoff simulation, terrain-based flow routing and
water-depth estimation into a single reproducible pipeline, built around
one project object that accumulates data and results as it flows through
the stages.

It is designed for teaching as much as for research: a companion
[floodflow
manual](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/manual/floodflow_manual.md)
explains every concept, derives the equations, and includes worked
exercises and projects, using the June 2026 Accra floods as a running
case study.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("gowusu/floodflow")
```

The core is pure R. Optional engines (`terra`, `airGR`, `extRemes`,
`ranger`, `whitebox`, `tmap`) add power to individual stages and are
loaded only when needed; if one is missing, the relevant function tells
you which package to install rather than failing obscurely.

## Quick start

A flood depth from a rainfall record in six lines:

``` r

library(floodflow)

fp <- flood_project("test")
fp$rainfall <- data.frame(date = Sys.Date() + 0:10,
                          precip_mm = c(0,0,0,20,50,30,10,0,0,0,0))
fp <- flood_runoff(fp, lat_deg = 5.6)
fp <- flood_route(fp, width = 25, slope = 0.002, area_km2 = 400)
fp$route$peak_depth_m        # ~2.07 m
```

## Pipeline

    flood_project()      # create the project (ingest DEM + rainfall)
    flood_extremes()     # fit stationary/non-stationary GEV; test for a trend
    flood_scenario()     # trend / delta / CMIP6 climate-adjusted design event
    roughness()          # Manning's n: constant, land cover, or NDVI
    flood_runoff()       # rainfall -> discharge
    flood_route()        # manning-normal / kinematic / diffusive / muskingum-cunge / dynamic
    flood_hydraulics()   # velocity, time of concentration, travel time
    flood_uncertainty()  # GLUE ensemble and inverse calibration
    flood_vulnerability()# hazard x exposure x vulnerability
    flood_surrogate()    # fast machine-learning emulator
    flood_map()          # interactive and side-by-side maps

## Design principles

- **Map-first.** Every stage returns something that can be rendered as a
  map: discharge, velocity, travel time, depth and risk.
- **Climate as a toggle.** Any flood scenario can be produced for a
  present-day or a climate-adjusted design event, side by side.
- **Built for scarce data.** Defaults use satellite or reanalysis
  rainfall, temperature-based evapotranspiration, and regional pooling
  of short records.
- **Honest about limits.** The `dynamic` routing method is a stable 1-D
  approximation, not full 2-D hydrodynamics; the simple runoff model is
  a mass-conserving translator, not a calibrated GR4J. These are stated,
  not hidden.

## Documentation

- [**Manual**](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/manual/floodflow_manual.md)
  — the full teaching guide, renders on GitHub. Theory boxes, worked
  equations, exercises and projects, and a spatial-mapping walkthrough.
  Built on the real bundled `accra_rainfall` record;
  `manual/reproduce_manual.R` regenerates every figure. A Word version
  (`manual/floodflow_manual.docx`) is there for a printable copy.
- [Documentation site](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/) — function
  reference and vignettes rendered as web pages.
- [Getting-started
  guide](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/GETTING-STARTED.md) — the
  full scenario matrix.
- Package help:
  [`?flood_route`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/flood_route.md),
  `example(flood_route)`, and `browseVignettes("floodflow")` after
  installation.

## Status

Version 0.1.0. All pipeline stages are implemented and tested (200+
internal checks). The core is pure R; geospatial and modelling engines
are optional and skip-guarded. External validation against gauged
catchments is the focus of the [v0.2
roadmap](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/floodflow_v0.2_roadmap.md).

## Citing floodflow

> Owusu, G. (2026). *floodflow: Climate-informed flood modelling in R.*
> Version 0.1.0. Department of Geography and Resource Development,
> University of Ghana.

# Package index

## Project and pipeline

- [`flood_project()`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/flood_project.md)
  : Create a flood project object
- [`is_flood_project()`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/is_flood_project.md)
  : Test whether an object is a flood project

## Rainfall extremes and climate scenarios

- [`flood_extremes()`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/flood_extremes.md)
  : Analyse rainfall extremes and test for a changing climate
- [`flood_scenario()`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/flood_scenario.md)
  : Generate a climate-adjusted design flood event

## Runoff, routing and hydraulics

- [`pet_oudin()`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/pet_oudin.md)
  : Potential evapotranspiration by the Oudin formula
- [`flood_runoff()`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/flood_runoff.md)
  : Simulate discharge from rainfall
- [`flood_route()`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/flood_route.md)
  : Route flow and compute water depth
- [`flood_hydraulics()`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/flood_hydraulics.md)
  : Derive hydraulic quantities from routed flow
- [`roughness()`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/roughness.md)
  : Assign Manning's roughness
- [`floodflow_lc_roughness`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/floodflow_lc_roughness.md)
  : Default Manning's roughness by land-cover class
- [`tc_kirpich()`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/tc_kirpich.md)
  : Time of concentration by the Kirpich method
- [`tc_kerby()`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/tc_kerby.md)
  : Time of concentration by the Kerby method (overland flow)

## Uncertainty, vulnerability and emulation

- [`flood_uncertainty()`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/flood_uncertainty.md)
  : Quantify uncertainty and invert for parameters (GLUE)
- [`flood_vulnerability()`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/flood_vulnerability.md)
  : Combine hazard, exposure and vulnerability into a risk index
- [`flood_surrogate()`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/flood_surrogate.md)
  : Train a fast surrogate emulator of the flood model

## Mapping

- [`flood_map()`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/flood_map.md)
  : Map a flood layer

## Data

- [`accra_rainfall`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/accra_rainfall.md)
  : Daily rainfall and temperature for Accra, Ghana (1981 to present)

## Print and summary methods

- [`print(`*`<flood_extremes>`*`)`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/print.flood_extremes.md)
  : Print a flood extremes result
- [`print(`*`<flood_hydraulics>`*`)`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/print.flood_hydraulics.md)
  : Print a flood hydraulics result
- [`print(`*`<flood_map>`*`)`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/print.flood_map.md)
  : Print a flood map
- [`print(`*`<flood_project>`*`)`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/print.flood_project.md)
  : Print a flood project
- [`print(`*`<flood_roughness>`*`)`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/print.flood_roughness.md)
  : Print a roughness result
- [`print(`*`<flood_route>`*`)`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/print.flood_route.md)
  : Print a flood route result
- [`print(`*`<flood_runoff>`*`)`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/print.flood_runoff.md)
  : Print a flood runoff result
- [`print(`*`<flood_scenario>`*`)`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/print.flood_scenario.md)
  : Print a flood scenario
- [`print(`*`<flood_surrogate>`*`)`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/print.flood_surrogate.md)
  : Print a flood surrogate
- [`print(`*`<flood_uncertainty>`*`)`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/print.flood_uncertainty.md)
  : Print a flood uncertainty result
- [`print(`*`<flood_vulnerability>`*`)`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/print.flood_vulnerability.md)
  : Print a flood vulnerability result
- [`summary(`*`<flood_project>`*`)`](https://gowusu.github.io/floodflow/reference/summary.flood_project.md)
  : Summarise a flood project
